captions.detailed: This 3D model is a decorative, hollow Easter egg featuring a complex lattice outer shell and a solid inner cup or partial shell. The outer lattice is made of intersecting curved bands that form diamond-shaped windows, creating an organic, woven structure. Inside the lattice, a smooth, angled container shell is visible, partially filling the lower half of the egg. The overall shape is elongated vertically, tapering more sharply at the top than at the bottom.
captions.instruction: Design a parametric decorative Easter egg in OpenSCAD with a customizable outer lattice pattern and an optional inner solid shell. The script should allow the user to control the egg width, the number of lattice loops, the loop style (single, double, or triple), and the height and tilt angle of the inner shell.
captions.factory: The code generates the egg by scaling a basic sphere differently on the top and bottom halves (using scale_z_top and scale_z_bottom) and joining them at the equator. The outer lattice is constructed using boolean intersection operations on a basic hollowed sphere, combined with rotated modules that define the loop geometry. The inner solid cup is formed by a partial sphere (basic_sphere_emboss) that is sliced at an angle using the emboss_tilt and emboss_ratio parameters.
